name: Garage Conversion vs New Detached ADU in Los Angeles

mainEntity.name: What are the pros and cons of converting a Los Angeles garage to living space versus building a new detached ADU from the ground up?
mainEntity.text: What are the pros and cons of converting a Los Angeles garage to living space versus building a new detached ADU from the ground up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing between converting an existing garage and building a new detached ADU in Los Angeles involves trade-offs in budget, layout, and site constraints. **Garage conversions** generally start with an existing shell and slab, often reducing framing and foundation costs. They can be quicker to build and may minimize new impervious area. However, many garages need substantial upgrades—new foundation edges, insulation, framing, and seismic reinforcement—to meet residential standards. Ceiling height, window locations, and structural elements can limit design flexibility. Driveway and parking changes may also be required. A **new detached ADU** costs more because it needs full foundations, framing, roofing, and utilities, along with site work and sometimes retaining walls or grading. Yet it offers a clean slate: better orientation for light and privacy, optimized room shapes, and modern energy performance. It can be easier to meet current setbacks and fire separation requirements on some lots. From a value perspective, both can add usable housing and potential rental income. A garage conversion may be the fastest way to create a unit on a tight budget, while a new ADU may provide a more durable, comfortable, and flexible long-term solution. A site-specific assessment by a contractor or designer is essential.
acceptedAnswer.description: Garage conversions usually cost less and use the existing footprint but may require significant structural upgrades and design compromises. New detached ADUs offer more layout freedom, better daylight, and modern foundations but cost more and need full site work, utilities, and new permitting.
